facts.value: Tries ftCo_SpecialS_CheckInput, ftCo_Attack100_CheckInput, ftCo_800D6824, ftCo_800D68C0, ftCo_Catch_CheckInput, ftCo_AttackS4_CheckInput, ftCo_AttackHi4_CheckInput, ftCo_AttackLw4_CheckInput, ftCo_AttackS3_CheckInput, ftCo_AttackHi3_CheckInput, ftCo_AttackLw3_CheckInput, ftCo_Attack1_CheckInput, ftCo_80091A4C, ftCo_800DE9D8, ftCo_Jump_CheckInput, ftCo_Dash_CheckInput, ftCo_800D5FB0, ftCo_Turn_CheckInput, then ftCo_Walk_CheckInput_Ottotto. Each receives unchanged gobj; the first nonzero result returns immediately. The second predicate dispatches ftData_SpecialHi, not rapid jab; the next two dispatch SpecialN and SpecialLw. Those three require a non-NULL table entry and zero x686, x689, or x687 respectively.
facts.rationale: Corrects the rapid-jab interpretation using active canonical dispatch while preserving exact priority.

evidence.why: Active special dispatch and optional branches.

facts.value: Delegates unchanged gobj to ftCo_Ottotto_IASA, sharing its complete first-nonzero interrupt priority without local guards or additional work. In that chain ftCo_Attack100_CheckInput dispatches ftData_SpecialHi rather than rapid jab; ftCo_800D6824 and ftCo_800D68C0 dispatch SpecialN and SpecialLw.
facts.rationale: Preserves shared processing while correcting the rapid-attack label.

facts.value: Enters ftCo_MS_OttottoWait when called by the initial Ottotto animation callback after its remaining-animation query returns false. It resets two fighter audio slots through ft_80088770 and ft_800887CC, then requests ft_80088328 with fp->ft_data->x4C_sfx->x18, volume 127, and pan 64. Actual audio submission depends on suppression/fighter-kind and sound-ID sentinel branches.
facts.rationale: Replaces generic setup and unconditional playback with verified audio behavior.

facts.value: Calls ftAnim_IsFramesRemaining with gobj. True causes no local transition; false calls ftCo_8009A6B8 with the same object to enter OttottoWait, reset two audio slots, and make a conditional sound request. There is no local timer or one-shot latch. The query also returns false when no eligible part reports remaining animation.
facts.rationale: Removes unsupported visual-effect initialization and clarifies the query boundary.

facts.value: Begins the initial Ottotto edge-balance/teeter phase when selected by the edge predicate. It selects ftCo_MS_Ottotto and clears self_vel.x/y/z and gr_vel. This establishes a self/ground-velocity reset, not the absence of every external or collision-driven motion source.
facts.rationale: Keeps the supported mapping without claiming total immobility.

evidence.why: Edge-triggered entry and exact velocity writes.

facts.value: Enters ftCo_MS_Ottotto with Ft_MF_None and transition arguments 0, 1, 0, NULL, then clears self_vel.x/y/z and gr_vel. Its local caller selects it when Collide_Edge intersects the environment flags and x2228_b2 is clear. The reset does not prove that the fighter's position remains stationary under other systems.
facts.rationale: Tightens the prior librarian's retained movement-arrest purpose to the operations actually proved.

evidence.why: Caller guard and complete entry body.
Separate collision processing writes current position.

facts.value: Occupies the initial Ottotto edge-balance/teeter physics slot with an empty callback. It adds no state-specific physics operation. Entry resets self and ground velocity, but global stationarity is not established; separate collision processing can update fighter position.
facts.rationale: Distinguishes local no-op physics from a global no-motion invariant.

evidence.why: Empty physics and separate collision phase.

facts.value: Maintains the sustained OttottoWait edge-balance/teeter phase against both floor support and facing-side endpoint distance. A false ft_800827A0 result calls ftCo_Fall_Enter. On success, distance strictly greater than x478+x47C calls ft_8008A2BC for conditional neutral-state recovery; otherwise this callback makes no additional state-changing call. Support alone is not sufficient to remain in OttottoWait.
facts.rationale: Repairs the prior retained mapping's omission of the supported-but-out-of-range exit.
